description:
FOUND s492a (Opus, 2026-09-20) writing the File::Copy acceptance probe for
#1999.  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00 (probed on a 268d7e00 extraction as
well as on the s492a tree).

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3;
scratch/s492a/probes/m5-tmpdir.pl in the s492a worktree):
  use File::Temp qw(tempdir);
  my $d = tempdir(CLEANUP => 1);
  print "dir=", (-d $d ? "ok" : "FAIL"), "\n";
  perl: dir=ok
  PCL:  Error in tempdir() using /tmp/XXXXXXXXXX:
        Parent directory (tmp) does not exist

`tempfile()` (the sibling) works, and so does `tempdir` with an explicit
DIR => "/tmp".  The message is File::Temp's own `_is_safe`/parent check, and
what it names as the parent is `tmp` -- a RELATIVE path -- where the template
it was handed is the ABSOLUTE `/tmp/XXXXXXXXXX`.  So the parent is being
derived from the template with the leading `/` lost: the suspect is PCL's
File::Spec splitdir/catdir on an absolute path inside File::Temp's
`_parent_dir`-style code, or the shim's `File::Spec->tmpdir`.

THE CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken): under ./runpcl print
  File::Spec->tmpdir, File::Spec->splitdir("/tmp/ABCDEF"),
  File::Spec->catdir(File::Spec->splitdir("/tmp/ABCDEF")[0..$#-1])
and compare with perl's -- one of them drops the leading empty segment that
makes a path absolute.

WHY IT MATTERS: `tempdir(CLEANUP => 1)` is the standard one-liner for a
scratch directory, in scripts and in test files alike, and File::Temp is on
the README's module list.  Every program that uses it dies at that line.

BAR: whichever layer the measurement names (File::Spec shim, File::Temp
shim, or a path primitive in cl/) => full sweep + guard rows in an existing
Pl/t file that make a tempdir and stat it, with perl as the oracle.
subject: EVERYDAY (File::Temp): `tempdir(CLEANUP => 1)` with no template DIES -- "Error in tempdir() using /tmp/XXXXXXXXXX: Parent directory (tmp) does not exist"
